_schema: Each row: id, class(live|filing|event), value, status(clear|amber|red|watch), proposed_status, rationale, confidence(high|medium|low), series_id, source, citation(URL), as_of(YYYY-MM-DD), next_release. RULES: (1) live/filing status is derived deterministically from value vs trigger. (2) event rows — the agent may self-promote clear->amber WITH a citation; amber->red and any de-escalation go in proposed_status for user confirm, never in status. (3) No citation => no status change on event/filing rows (the console rejects it). (4) confidence defaults to 'medium' if unstated. (5) reputable secondary sources (Reuters/BBG/FT) are acceptable when the primary isn't out yet.
_paste_note: The agent writes only the mutable fields (value, status, proposed_status, rationale, confidence, citation, as_of, next_release). The console holds the static definitions (names, conditions, guardrails, trigger). Paste this whole object, or just a {"asOf":..,"posture":..,"rows":[..]} with the ids you changed.

rows.trigger: RED: 2+ of MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/META guide capex DOWN YoY. AMBER: AI credit stress (CDS/spreads widening) + compute/memory pricing rolling over together.
rows.rationale: All four raised at Q2 rather than cut: AMZN ~$200B → ~$220B on higher memory cost, GOOGL $180–190B → $195–205B to accelerate capacity, META floor up to $130–145B, MSFT ~$175B purely on a finance→operating lease reclass with the underlying build unchanged — the red test (2+ guiding capex DOWN YoY) is not close. Cloud second derivative is still positive: Azure 40% → 43%, AWS +37% (fastest in 18 quarters), Google Cloud +82%, Microsoft commercial RPO $678B (+84%). Amber needs credit stress AND compute/memory pricing rolling over together: the credit leg is live (NVDA 5y CDS at a record 82bp on 7/27 and 77bp on 8/10, spread over Treasuries doubled since June, CoreWeave loan spreads +125bp, Oracle cut to the bottom investment-grade notch) but the pricing leg is absent — advanced packaging is sold out through 2026 and memory is inflating capex, not deflating it. One leg, not two.

rows.trigger: RED: central banks shift to sustained NET SELLING of gold. Not ETF flows/price/USD.
rows.value: official sector net buyer — record Q2 at 289t
rows.rationale: WGC Gold Demand Trends (published 7/30, first read for this row) puts Q2 central-bank net purchases at 288.9t: +62% YoY, the strongest Q2 on record and more than five times the revised 57t Q1. Poland +51t, China +33t (its biggest quarter since late 2023), Uzbekistan +16t, Kazakhstan +15t. The cohort is uneven — Russia sold 22t to plug its budget, Turkey and Azerbaijan also net sellers, and H1's 345t is the lowest since 2022 — but uneven buying is not the red test, which needs sustained net SELLING. 89% of surveyed reserve managers expect official gold reserves to keep growing.
rows.next_release: Q3 2026 WGC Gold Demand Trends (late Oct)

rows.trigger: RED: Core PCE <=~2% for 2-3 consecutive quarters WHILE real policy positive AND real yields falling.
rows.rationale: Core PCE index 130.266 for June = 3.3% YoY, nowhere near the ≤~2% red line, and the Fed's 7/29 statement still calls inflation elevated with energy supply shocks in the mix. Real policy is positive (DFII10 +2.40%) but real yields are RISING, not falling (2.24% on 7/06 → 2.40% on 8/07), so neither half of the red condition — disinflation, and falling real yields alongside positive real policy — is present. Regime assumption under the scarcity leg holds.

rows.trigger: RED: sustained organic growth <~10-12% across core compounders OR structural NRR fall.
rows.rationale: NOW subscription revenue +24.5% YoY with cRPO +21%, 123 net-new-ACV deals over $1M (+40% YoY) and FY26 guidance raised; SHOP revenue +33.7% and accelerating on GMV +31.6%, with merchant retention 92% above $1M GMV and 97% above $10M; SAP cloud +22%. The serial acquirers run low organic by design, not by decay — TOI Q2 organic 4% on +18% total revenue (reported 8/05), CSU Q1 organic 2% FX-neutral inside a 1–4% band that has held for nine quarters — so 'sustained <10–12% ACROSS core compounders' is not met. Gaps to close: CSU's own Q2 is still pending, and neither CRM nor SNOW has disclosed NRR for the quarter.

rows.trigger: AMBER: vol uncompressing / dispersion->correlation / cross-sector stress / disorderly USDJPY. Bucket C deploy: correlation event or SOXX -30% ($459.20). Action is inverted: protect ballast.
rows.value: carry unwind — USD/JPY 157.54, VIX back to 14.9
rows.rationale: Clustered signals, not one: Japan's largest-ever yen intervention around 7/30 (US participation unconfirmed) took USD/JPY from 163.86 to 157.44 inside five sessions, including a −2.3% day on 8/03 that repriced everything carry-funded at once — EUR/JPY −2.1%, AUD/JPY −2.5%, WTI −6.4%, gold −0.7% — against a VIX spike to 20.66 on 7/29 and a margin-called fund force-selling AI-infra names on 7/30. That is disorderly USDJPY plus cross-asset deleveraging in one window. The acute phase has passed: VIX 14.9, SPX 7753 near highs, DGS10 easing to 4.65%, and stock–bond correlation is not currently broken. So this is alertness, not a Bucket C event — protect the ballast, do not pre-spend it. Watch whether carry funding rotates into CHF/EUR now that the BoJ has drawn a line.

rows.trigger: AMBER Tier1 (any one): explicit YCC / non-crisis QE (WALCL up while core PCE>target) / SLR exemption. Tier2 (need 2+): bill share >~25% marketable debt / stablecoin bill demand scaling. Falsifiers: DFII10 positive, fiscal consolidation, hawk bloc.
rows.value: no Tier-1 fire; hawk bloc active — but WALCL +$143B in 26 weeks
rows.rationale: Falsifiers are holding hard, which is why status stays clear: the 7/29 FOMC held 3.50–3.75% on a 9–3 vote with Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissenting FOR a 25bp hike, the statement says flatly 'The Committee will deliver price stability', DFII10 is durably positive at +2.40%, and the 8/05 QRA left coupon and FRN auction sizes unchanged with the bill share at 22.2% — under the ~25% Tier-2 line. What argues the other way, and why I am proposing amber rather than asserting it: WALCL has expanded in every month of 2026, +$13B over four weeks and +$142.7B over 26 weeks to $6.749T, while core PCE runs 3.3% and there is no crisis — the literal Tier-1 'non-crisis QE' reading. The benign explanation is in the statement itself ('continuing its policy of maintaining ample reserves') and in a directive that buys bills for reserve management rather than stimulus. Stablecoin bill demand is scaling ($308.5B, OCC implementing GENIUS via 12 CFR Part 15) but that is one Tier-2 leg and Tier 2 needs two. Your call on which reading governs; accepting this puts gold-weight on the table.

rows.trigger: RED: ASML credible Chinese EUV >80-90% yield pre-2030; AMAT/LRCX China etch/dep share ~60% or tool-of-record; KLA China process-control share ~20% (canary); MU CXMT ships HBM3E/4 to major vendor or China HBM >10% of bits.
rows.value: no threshold crossed — EUV moat intact, KLA canary quiet
rows.rationale: A confirmed development that crosses none of the four red lines. State-backed Shanghai Aishengna has begun producing domestic immersion DUV — a first — with ~5 units this year to SMIC, Hua Hong and CXMT for line validation and ~20 planned for 2027, against ASML's ~130 immersion units of 2026 capacity; SemiAnalysis reads it as displacing revenue export controls already took from ASML. EUV is untouched: the Shenzhen prototype generates photons but has not exposed a wafer. CXMT listed on 7/27 (+466%, ~$9.8B raised) at ~8% DRAM share but has no qualified HBM product and no disclosed shipments — targeting HBM3/HBM3E from end-2026 with thermal and yield problems, one to two generations behind HBM4 — so the MU leg is not live. Process control, KLA's ground and the designated canary, is where China is furthest behind. Proposing amber anyway because Naura is now the world's #5 toolmaker with backlog into 2027, ahead of KLA, and China's ≥50% domestic-sourcing mandates aim straight at the AMAT/LRCX etch/dep leg well before the ~60% line.
rows.next_release: event-driven · watch Aishengna line qualification at SMIC/CXMT

rows.trigger: Falsify: 2Y sustained >4.25% + USD breaking higher, not lower.
rows.rationale: Neither leg of the falsifier is complete, but both are close. DGS2 at 4.19% sits 6bp under the sustained-4.25% line. DXY at 99.75 is rangebound 99–101: it printed a 2026 high just over 99.68 and a seven-week low of 99.42 on 8/03 after the yen intervention, so the dollar is resilient rather than breaking either way — held up by Middle East safe-haven demand and a live hike premium. Peak-hawkishness is the harder half of the call to defend: three FOMC members voted for a hike on 7/29 and the market prices at least one 2026 hike, not the cuts this framework needs.

rows.trigger: Falsify: Fed tightens into disinflation & holds; real yields break out, no repression.
rows.value: debasement plumbing intact — no disinflation to tighten into
rows.rationale: The falsifier needs the Fed tightening into disinflation while real yields break out with no repression. There is no disinflation to tighten into — core PCE 3.3% with a Hormuz energy shock feeding it — and the plumbing still leans his way: WALCL +$142.7B over 26 weeks, the 8/05 QRA freezing coupon and FRN sizes so incremental funding goes to bills, and a $308.5B stablecoin complex as a structural bill bid. The pressure worth tracking is real yields firming (DFII10 2.24% → 2.40% since early July) with a committee that has three votes for a hike; that is the falsifier's second leg forming without its first.

rows.trigger: Falsify: diversification holds through a deleveraging (bonds rally as equities fall).
rows.rationale: The falsifier — bonds rally as equities fall — did not happen in the one deleveraging we got. On 7/29 the S&P fell 1.5% to 7316 while DGS10 ROSE to 4.67%, and kept rising to 4.75% by 7/31; gold also fell 0.7% into the 8/03 carry unwind. Treasuries sold with equities, so correlation-to-one held and the framework stands. It cuts the same way on the recovery: the 8/03–8/10 rally lifted stocks and bonds together, which is the same correlation with the sign flipped. Cross-ref tw6.

rows.trigger: Falsify: value stays at model layer; open-weights fail to commoditize.
rows.value: margin still migrating to the supply chain
rows.rationale: The falsifier is value staying at the model layer, and it isn't. Hyperscaler capex is up ~80% YoY toward $720–745B, and the scarce links are the ones setting price: Amazon lifted its 2026 guide ~$20B explicitly on higher memory cost, advanced packaging is sold out through 2026, and token economics face upward input-cost pressure rather than the usual silicon deflation. Model-layer output is being funded by the infrastructure layer and increasingly priced by it. Open-weight commoditization is the leg I have no fresh read on this week.

rows.trigger: Falsify: oil supply surprises to the upside; backwardation fails to appear.
rows.value: steep backwardation — supply not surprising higher
rows.rationale: Falsifier decisively absent. The curve is in pronounced backwardation — Brent Oct-26 $83.6 against Dec-26 $80.0 on 8/07, WTI Sep-26 $78.2 against Dec-26 $74.6, and a late-July WTI M1–M12 spread near $15 — with roughly 8.5 mb/d of Q2 global inventory draw and thin Cushing stocks underneath it. Supply is undershooting, not surprising to the upside: OPEC+ added only ~188 kb/d for September to complete the 3.5 mb/d unwind, and physical Gulf exports run ~40% below pre-war levels behind the partially closed Strait of Hormuz. The live risk to the thesis is demand destruction at these prices, not new barrels.

rows.trigger: Falsify: committee acts on a real, sustained hawkish hike path.
rows.value: three dissents FOR a hike; median dot 3.8%
rows.rationale: Self-promoting clear → amber: the falsifier is a committee acting on a real, sustained hawkish hike path, and it is now one meeting from acting. The 7/29 hold was 9–3 with Hammack, Kashkari and Logan voting for +25bp; the statement says 'The Committee will deliver price stability'; nine of eighteen June dots had rates higher by year-end with the median up to 3.8% from 3.4%; forward guidance has been abolished and Warsh submits no dot of his own; the market prices a hike as soon as September. Not falsified — no hike has been delivered and DFF is still 3.63% — but the good-cop reading is carrying less of the explanation each meeting.
